The round-7 change is the demotion I asked for and it landed: `vocab_utilization` is now `_meta_vocab_utilization`, and its basis reproduces exactly -- over 18 tokenizers I measure pearson(vocab_utilization, 1/vocab_size) = +0.9953 (recorded +0.9955) and pearson with vocab_size itself -0.9302. The docstring's 'four top-25 partial predictors' claim is corrected in place with an explicit 2026-09-05 note saying every emitted key is already excluded by the analysis pipeline, which I re-verified against feature_selection.is_excluded_predictor: fertility, token_entropy and vocab_size all return True (excluded via TOKENIZER_PROXY_TERMS).
comparable_reason: The corpus is FIXED across models, so this task measures the tokenizer and nothing else, and three of its keys are one number rescaled: over 18 tokenizers pearson(fertility, _meta_compression_ratio) = 1.000000000000 and pearson(fertility, _meta_total_tokens) = 1.000000000000, with _meta_total_words = 1400 and _meta_total_chars = 7192 constant (std exactly 0) on every model. Resolution is also poor: 6 distinct fertility values over 18 tokenizers, so a regression on this column is regressing on tokenizer FAMILY, not on a graded property.
github_reason: hgiyt is the source of the 'fertility' definition (tokens per whitespace word) and BLME computes exactly that; there is no released script that produces a comparable per-model number on a fixed corpus, so this is a definition match, not an executed head-to-head.
paper_reason: Rust et al. publish fertility per LANGUAGE for monolingual vs multilingual BERT on their own corpora, not a value for GPT-2-family tokenizers on WikiText, so there is no reproducible scalar. GPT-2's fertility of 1.2093-1.2593 on English WikiText is in the right neighbourhood for an English-trained BPE but is not a published figure.
confounds_reason: By construction: `vocab_size` is emitted directly (rho +0.997 with the config's vocab_size, i.e. it IS the architecture parameter), and `_meta_vocab_utilization` is +0.9953 with 1/vocab_size. `token_entropy` carries rho -0.432 with vocab_size and -0.486 with n_layers. Every key is excluded by the analysis pipeline, so none of this reaches the regression -- which is the point the corrected docstring now makes.
defects: The corrected docstring says 'every one of the NINE keys this task emits'; the return dict has TEN keys (fertility, _meta_compression_ratio, token_entropy, _meta_normalised_token_entropy, _meta_vocab_utilization, vocab_size, _meta_entropy_ceiling_n, _meta_total_tokens, _meta_total_words, _meta_total_chars). Cosmetic, but the sentence is a count claim in a correction notice.

The normalized twin still does not normalize: pearson(_meta_normalised_token_entropy, token_entropy) = +0.8888 over 18 tokenizers, because the divisor log(min(T,V)) is log(T) for every model here and T ranges only 1693-1763 (a 4% span). It is correctly `_meta_`, so it is inert, but it is not a normalization.
